question.worked_solution:
From the identity $1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta $ with $\theta =x-\frac{\pi }{4},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}1+{cot}^{2}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4}) & ={csc}^{2}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\ {cot}^{2}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4}) & ={csc}^{2}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4}(1-{cot}^{2}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4}))\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4}(1-{csc}^{2}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4}(2-{csc}^{2}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4}))\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4}2\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4}{csc}^{2}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2x{|}_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4}+\operatorname{cot}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4}){|}_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4} \\  & =2(\frac{3\pi }{4}-\frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4}-\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =2(\frac{\pi }{4})+\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}+0-1 \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}-1.\end{aligned}
$$
